rules.value: Company and products are consistently referred to as 'Barco' under the master brand approach; no sub-branding or product logos.
rules.note: Brand architecture is based on customer impact, not company structure.

rules.value: Barco
rules.note: Use Barco as often as possible instead of division or legal entity names, in both external and internal communication.

rules.value: Use the legal entity name only in materials/documents with legal implications (e.g., address fields on invoices, letters, business cards).
rules.note: Applies to stationery and legally binding documents.

rules.value: Division, business unit, or location names can only be used combined with the Barco name, and only when the organizational structure matters.
rules.note: Applies to both external and internal communication.

rules.value: In external communication materials like brochures, ads, newsletters, magazines, refer simply to 'Barco' without division, market, or location, e.g. 'Barco introduces new LED display.'
rules.note: Division references reserved for specific communications like investor/analyst/press materials.

rules.value: When referencing a division/business unit/location/facility, always add the qualifying word ('division,' 'business unit,' 'location,' or 'facility') to clarify relationship to Barco.
rules.note: e.g. 'President of Barco's Entertainment division.'

rules.value: Visioneering a bright tomorrow
rules.note: Brand mantra used when communicating about Barco overall.

rules.value: Visioneering Healthcare, Visioneering Enterprise, Visioneering Entertainment
rules.note: Terms used when referring to Barco's markets/segments.

rules.value: Inspirational 'What if' or 'Imagine' statements
rules.note: Used when talking about segments, e.g. 'What if meetings could be truly inclusive?', 'Imagine diagnosing patients before they get sick.'

rules.value: Natural, everyday-speech writing style
rules.note: Barco's writing style is based on natural, conversational language.

rules.value: Fancy oratorical touches, bureaucratic phrases, or explicit commercial wording
rules.note: These are explicitly excluded from Barco's writing style.

rules.value: Write from an outcomes point of view
rules.note: Always find the outcome for the customer that will draw attention.

rules.value: Warm, open, personal tone using first- and second-person address ('we'/'you')
rules.note: Readers should feel personally addressed rather than spoken about impersonally.

rules.value: Barco / the customer (impersonal third-person reference)
rules.note: Avoid referring to company or reader in impersonal third person when a personal alternative is natural.

rules.value: colour
rules.note: British spelling forbidden in favor of American English per Cambridge Dictionary standard.

rules.value: grey
rules.note: British spelling forbidden in favor of American English.

rules.value: visualisation
rules.note: British spelling forbidden in favor of American English.

rules.value: centre
rules.note: British spelling forbidden in favor of American English.

rules.value: programme
rules.note: British spelling forbidden in favor of American English.

rules.value: Prefer active voice over passive voice
rules.note: e.g. 'A buys B' rather than 'B is bought by A.'

rules.value: Jargon in writing for a wide audience
rules.note: Avoid technical jargon in press releases, company introductions, market brochures; explain jargon on first use if necessary; technical terms acceptable only for specialist audiences.

rules.value: Short, frequently used words and simple sentence constructions
rules.note: Important since much of the audience is non-native English speakers; avoid long paragraphs.

rules.value: Maximum sentence length of 25 words
rules.note: Aim for concise sentences.

rules.value: We decided / I intend
rules.note: Simpler phrasing preferred over wordier constructions.
rules.related_term: We made a decision / I have the intention

rules.value: Abbreviations written in full on first appearance with abbreviation in brackets, unless the abbreviation is more common than the full form.
rules.note: Applies to non-acronym abbreviations.

rules.value: Acronyms formed from first letters are written in all capitals (e.g. NATO).
rules.note: Distinguished from pronounceable word-abbreviations.

rules.value: Abbreviations composed of word parts that can be pronounced as words are written as plain text (e.g. Unicef).
rules.note: Not written in all caps.

rules.value: Numerals one to ten spelled in words except for page references and percentages; numerals 11 and above, decimals, and fractions written in figures.
rules.note: e.g. 'Two contracts,' 'Page 3,' '8%,' '24 displays.'

rules.value: Phone and fax numbers written as +country code, area code, number (e.g. +32 56 123 456).
rules.note: Do not use format like '0032 56 123 456.'

rules.value: Dates written consistently as day/month/year (e.g. '3 June 2004' or 'June 3, 2003').
rules.note: Avoid ordinal suffixes like '3rd June 2003.'

rules.value: In running text, place currency symbol before the figure with no space; 'million' can be abbreviated to 'm'; 'billion' always spelled out. If currency symbol omitted, currency word follows the figure.
rules.note: e.g. currency-250 million, currency-250m, currency-32 billion, 32 billion euro.

rules.value: Headlines should be active, present tense, and short (preferably no more than two lines).
rules.note: Applies to titles and headlines.

rules.value: Titles in brochures and communication tools use initial cap only for the first word of the title.
rules.note: Standard spelling rules for titles.

rules.value: Barco is always written in lower case with a capital B; never in full caps.
rules.note: Applies to all uses including copyright notices.

rules.value: BARCO (full caps)
rules.note: Avoid writing Barco in all capital letters.

rules.value: 'Visioneering a bright tomorrow' is written in lower case with a capital V.
rules.note: Consistent capitalization rule for the brand mantra.

rules.value: Copyright notices contain the copyright symbol, year of first publication, and owner, e.g. '(c) 2023, Barco.'
rules.note: Barco remains lower case with capital B in copyright notices.

rules.value: Product naming offers three possibilities: fully descriptive name, compound word highlighting USPs, or product code.
rules.note: e.g. Barco Canvas, ClickShare, Barco UniSee.

rules.value: Precede product names with 'Barco' to gain basic name protection and reinforce brand association.
rules.note: Reinforces position as a Barco product in the market.

rules.value: Barco is a branded house; only the Barco name and logo are trademarked. Product/service names use descriptive (compound) names or product codes, not registered as trademarks except in exceptional cases.
rules.note: Exceptions include crown jewel products, competitive necessity, new market entries, or inherited trademarks from acquisitions (e.g. UniSee, Demetra, Nexxis, Eonis, ClickShare, wePresent).

rules.value: Confident and future-facing
rules.note: Barco's marketing comes across as confident and future-facing, per fan observation of their messaging and press releases.

rules.value: Inspirational, almost sci-fi, using big 'what if' style questions
rules.note: Brand frequently poses aspirational 'what if' questions (e.g., 'what if surgery could happen from anywhere'), giving an inspirational, slightly sci-fi tone.

rules.value: visioneering
rules.note: Barco uses this coined term (a mashup of 'vision' + 'engineering') in its marketing language.

rules.value: Barco
rules.note: Brand refers to itself simply as 'Barco' rather than using long corporate-speak division names, except in investor-relations documents; reflects a 'one brand' approach rather than house-of-brands.

rules.value: Plain, matter-of-fact writing with short sentences, not flowery
rules.note: Observed writing style avoids flowery language and uses short, matter-of-fact sentences.

rules.value: Not jargon-heavy even for technical products
rules.note: Even when discussing technical products like projectors and LED walls, the writing avoids heavy jargon.

rules.value: inspirational
rules.note: Autumn campaign copy can lean slightly more inspirational, as long as it still follows the standard tone-of-voice rules.

rules.value: What if" framing
rules.note: Suggested inspirational framing device for autumn campaign messaging.

rules.value: Visioneering
rules.note: Suggested inspirational language for autumn campaign messaging.

rules.value: Barco
rules.note: Use with a capital B and rest lower case; never use full caps, per capitalization rule in main guide.

rules.value: BARCO
rules.note: Full caps version of the brand name should never be used, per capitalization rule.
